_notes: Labeled set for eval_tool_selection.py. Each entry has a 'question' plus exactly one of: 'expected_tool' (single required tool), 'expected_tools' (ordered list, for legitimate multi-step chains like search_awards -> get_award_details - scored twice: tool_selection_correct asks only that all of them appear, tool_order_correct that they appear in this order, with unrelated calls in between allowed), or 'acceptable_tools' (any one of these counts as a pass - for the 'ambiguous_intentional' category, where more than one tool is a defensible choice).

'confusable_with' (optional) lists the specific alternative tool(s) this question is structurally similar to - if the agent calls one of these instead of/alongside the expected tool, it's tallied in the confusion report even on entries that otherwise pass.

'then_one_of' (optional, paired with 'expected_tools') - a second step where more than one tool is a legitimate choice (e.g. resolve_naics_code -> either search_awards or get_spending_by_category both correctly use the resolved code). AND'd onto expected_tools: all of expected_tools must appear, AND at least one of then_one_of must also appear - and for tool_order_correct, after the last expected_tools entry.

'check_hedge_language' (optional, bool) flags entries where a resolve_*_code tool presents a code to the user - scored informationally (diagnostic, not gating overall pass/fail) on whether the final answer hedges appropriately (e.g. 'closest match', 'semantic match', 'verify') rather than stating the code as a confirmed fact.

'expected_args' (optional) maps a tool name to the arguments that call must have been made with, scored as tool_args_correct. A scalar must match (case-insensitive, string-coerced), a list means any one of them is fine, and "<from:some_tool>" means the value must appear in an earlier some_tool call's output - that's the check that a resolved code was actually used rather than guessed. Only grades tools the run actually called, so a then_one_of entry can name args for either branch; whether a tool was called at all is tool_selection_correct's job. Only assert args whose wrong value would make the answer wrong.

'expect_failure_acknowledged' (optional, bool) marks an error_paths entry - a deliberately broken input that should drive a tool into its "This query failed" or no-results branch. Scored twice: tool_failure_observed checks deterministically that a tool really did return a failure (if the live API changes and the input starts working, the case has stopped testing anything and this says so), and failure_acknowledged asks an LLM judge whether the answer owned up to it rather than quietly substituting other data. The judge is diagnostic, not gating, until calibrate_failure_judge.py measures it.
category is filled in by eval_tool_selection.py from the top-level key, not stored per-entry.
